newsitem.title: USA: Sperling says Republican budget unacceptable.
newsitem.headline: Sperling says Republican budget unacceptable.

text.p: The White House still has serious objections to the tax cutting packages moving through both the Senate and House of Representatives, National Economic Council chairman Gene Sperling said Sunday.

Sperling, interviewed on CNN's Late Edition, said the Senate version, which won considerable Democratic support when moving through the Senate Finance Committee, was slightly less objectionable than the House version.
Both bills now need approval from the full Senate and House before representatives of both chambers sit down together to hammer out a unified version.
"We do have serious concerns and we are going to press them on the floor and in conference to ensure we get a bill the president signs," Sperling said.
He said the White House would insist that the bill provided for social justice. In its present form, the richest one percent of the population benefited more than the bottom 60 per cent.
Clinton also wanted every family to benefit from a tax credit, whereas Republicans would deny the credits to families who did not pay income tax because their income was too low.
